title: AI agents build 3D scenes from photos but have no idea if they got it right
key_facts: LEGO-Anything, from researchers at the University of Maryland and AWS, has coding agents turn a single photo into an editable Blender scene by writing code, running it, inspecting the result and revising.
The accompanying LEGO-Bench holds 208 images from 104 indoor and outdoor scenes with 443 registered assets, rendered from professionally built simulator scenes so exact geometry is known for scoring.
Scenes are scored on validity, reconstruction accuracy and appearance.

All six tested GPT configurations almost always produced a working scene, but accuracy varied: GPT-6 Astra scored 53.4 percent indoors and 39.6 percent outdoors; weaker setups around 15 percent. More reasoning budget raised Astra's office-subset score from 32.3 to 61.8 percent.
When asked which of two versions better matched the photo, the models' geometric judgments were near or below chance, so agents cannot tell whether their own scene improved.

A training-free add-on, LEGO-Plugin, replaces self-judgment with measurements and protects progress from regressive edits, improving all six models, by up to 62.7 percent for weaker ones and about two points for the top model.
Reconstructed scenes used for object detection reached roughly half the performance of the specialised model DINO; segmentation and depth lagged further.
quote_evidence: GPT-6 Astra, the best tested model, hit 53.4 percent on indoor scenes and 39.6 percent on outdoor scenes.
When models had to pick which of two versions better matched the original, their geometric judgments landed near or below chance level.
The plugin improved all six models. Weaker agents saw the biggest gains, with boosts up to 62.7 percent.
why_it_matters_hint: A new benchmark shows coding agents can build 3D scenes from a photo but cannot judge their own accuracy, so refinement must rest on measurements, not model opinion.
notes: Research paper with no peer review mentioned; only GPT models tested. The Decoder's own reporting.
